determinism.request_identity: canonical project, resolved PV, lane, query, retrieval, and limit
determinism.result_order: input request index then source rank
determinism.result_identity: project, resolved PV, lane, ref, path, locator, source SHA, and chunk SHA

failure_and_cancellation.pending_cancellation: best-effort future cancellation with sealed CANCELLED status
failure_and_cancellation.timeout: sealed TIMEOUT status with no authority widening
failure_and_cancellation.worker_error: sealed ERROR status without hiding successful sibling lanes

verification.selector: Parallel query determinism, dedupe, budgets, cancellation, errors, schema parity, and immutable-PV integration
Lane guidance, reader, lane contract, registry, and packaged-skill integration
Python lint, compile, schema parse, and whitespace validation
verification.result: Ruff, py_compile, json.tool, and git diff --check passed

negative_cases: More than eight lane requests, more than four workers, or invalid per-lane limits and timeouts fail closed before execution.
A lane alias is canonicalized through the registry; it cannot select an arbitrary SQLite file or FTS table.
All requests bind to one resolved immutable PV; caller aliases cannot produce mixed-PV aggregate evidence.
Duplicate normalized requests execute once, and duplicate result identities do not inflate the aggregate.
Worker completion timing cannot change request receipts, result ordering, or aggregate receipt identity.
Timeout, cancellation, and worker error do not widen authority, mutate a lane, or discard successful sibling receipts.
No whole lane database, Plan backlog, PV package, or raw FTS corpus is placed in model context.
limitations: Row216 supplies the internal deterministic fan-out primitive; typed cross-lane joins remain Row217.
Explicit cross-project authority sets remain Row218.
Public skill and MCP action routing for the primitive remains owned by Row221.
next_boundary: Close Row216 through its exact per-Delta checkpoint. Row217 EL-CODEX-T6-PARITY-020-CROSS-LANE-QUERY owns typed joins across explicitly selected lanes without unrestricted SQL.
